proposal.angle: WebOps Factory gives small web teams a visible, reviewable path from supported static-site findings to a checked repair candidate—complete with before-and-after evidence and an exact patch—while leaving approval and deployment to people. Position it as a bounded review workflow, not an autonomous fixer or installation tutorial. Evidence: readme; verification.
outline: Lead with the reader problem: small teams need to fix website issues without losing visibility or control.
Introduce the benefit: WebOps Factory works on a copied static site, moves supported findings through specialist repair and independent review, and retains evidence for reviewers. [sourceId: readme]
Show the visible factory floor: handoffs, proposed values, reasons, screenshots, reports, and statuses backed by retained run records. [sourceId: readme]

Define the current boundary: four supported repair types—titles, search descriptions, missing alt attributes, and broken internal file links—while other reported findings remain visible. [sourceId: readme]

Use the recorded example as evidence, not a promise: five supported findings across three pages were repaired in 43.443 seconds with four provider calls; checks passed and the final state was approval_required, not deployed. [sourceId: verification]

Explain reviewer control: the original site remains unchanged; reviewers can inspect the candidate, exact patch, before-and-after findings, browser artifacts, independent review, and hashed package. [sourceId: readme; verification]

Close with the reader promise: gain a focused, inspectable repair candidate without handing deployment authority to the system. Direct readers to the repository README for complete prerequisites and setup.
risks: Do not imply broad site repair, perfect SEO, WCAG conformance, security certification, ranking gains, revenue gains, or production readiness; the supported checks are explicitly bounded.
Treat 43.443 seconds and all setup or portability timings as observations from specific recorded conditions, never performance or onboarding promises.
State clearly that the factory handles static exports, does not edit the original site, and neither approves nor deploys changes.
Do not reproduce commands, configuration fragments, or partial setup steps; link to the README instead.
The demo’s listening review is incomplete, and phone playback was checked through browser emulation rather than a physical device. Avoid stronger media-quality claims. [sourceId: verification]
Any claim beyond the captured README and verification record remains unverified and should be omitted or labeled uncertain.
